policy.admission: normal pressure, no new swap-outs, load1 <=5, no competing Go tools for 60 seconds

outcome.trigger: occupied swap grew beyond the experimental limit; stopped owned workload

conclusions: Allowing bounded swap let the broad command continue past the original first-swap-out stop, but it still did not finish within the approved resource envelope.
At the first sample beyond the cap, total occupied swap was approximately 2.33 GiB, growth approximately 2.07 GiB above the 267.25 MiB baseline.
The 70.75 MiB observed overshoot reflects a sampled monitor, not an OS-enforced allocation limit; the workload was stopped on the first observed exceedance.

Approximately 6.27 GiB of swap-out and 4.26 GiB of swap-in page-counter equivalents were recorded after prelaunch. These are system-wide page volumes, not uniquely attributed test pages or exact physical SSD I/O.
Normal OS pressure persisted despite substantial two-way paging; a normal pressure label alone does not establish acceptable test performance.
The approximately 8.33 GiB sampled process-tree RSS peak excludes swapped-out pages and is not the full test memory demand or a universal RAM minimum.
No failed assertion or timeout was reported before interruption, but the probe completed zero broad commands and cannot be reported as a test pass.
Further older-Mac experimentation should separately evaluate reducing peak live test memory or smaller process groups, rather than automatically increasing swap tolerance.
The earlier complete 32 GiB partition pass remains valid. No permanent swap policy, source assertion, package timeout or background setting was changed.
